headline: Red Sox win streak ends at nine after tough loss to Athletics
morning_brew: Well, the streak had to end sometime, but watching it go up in smoke at Fenway last night was like finding a cold cup of Dunks on the dashboard. The Athletics took us down 7-3, and it felt like we were playing catch-up from the second inning on. I was ready to celebrate a second double-digit win streak this season, but instead, we looked about as sharp as a butter knife. My ma watched the first few innings and just sighed, telling me we looked like we were swinging at beach balls in the dark. She is always right, and last night, the bats just lacked that electric fire we have been riding for the last week.

Bennett struggled to keep things in the yard, exiting in the sixth after coughing up four runs, and the arson squad took over soon after to make sure the game stayed firmly in the loss column. It is a nauseating result, especially when you consider how high the energy has been in the Hub lately. I have been saying it all year, this team lives and dies by that early adrenaline, and when the starter doesn't give us the length we need, the whole house of cards starts to wobble. My neighbor Rick is already drafting an umpire conspiracy dossier because of some of those calls, but I told him to put the pen away and focus on the fact that we have a chance to flush this one today before we head to Toronto.

Elsewhere, the off-season noise surrounding the Celtics and Bruins continues to be a total headache, but at least we aren't having to talk about the 76ers or the Sabres today. It is a quiet, grumpy morning in the Hub while we wait for first pitch at Fenway. We are still right in the mix, and one bad night doesn't erase the fact that this team has been playing some of the best baseball in the league for the last two weeks. Time to turn the page and get back to business.

news_digest.headline: Athletics end Red Sox's bid for second 10-game win streak
news_digest.dans_take: Nine in a row was a hell of a ride, but nobody wants to be the one holding the bag when the music stops.

news_digest.headline: Olney on Red Sox: This is the 'craziest team turnaround in the history of baseball'
news_digest.dans_take: It is nice to get the national love, but I would trade every highlight reel on TV for one more win in the standings.

trend_watch.dans_take: He ate some innings when we needed the help, but watching the lead balloon in the late frames was enough to make me change the channel.

trend_watch.trend: Five and a third innings, four earned runs
trend_watch.dans_take: That wasn't the command we have come to expect, and against a team like Oakland, you simply cannot be handing out free passes like candy.
Nice to see him find a gap, but it was like bringing an umbrella to a monsoon — way too little, way too late.
